item.title: Tech Ledger | Orders for mining equipment hold steady
item.description: Order books at the largest suppliers were flat against a strong comparison period.
item.content:encoded:
Dealers said Caterpillar took the biggest share of new truck orders.

Analysts said Caterpillar would keep pricing firm through the year.

One dealer said Caterpillar delivery times had shortened to nine months.

Shipments to dealers rose 4 percent on the quarter.

Rebuild work at Caterpillar dealers rose 7 percent, the dealers said.

item.title: Furnace restart adds jobs at the mill
item.description: Local officials said the hiring will begin next month at the site.
item.content:encoded:
The steelmaker said in a statement that the second furnace restarted on schedule and will reach full output by the end of April.

It said the maintenance programme cost 60 million dollars and added 40 permanent jobs at the site.

The plant manager said the older furnace would stay idle until demand improves.

item.title: Alphabet opens a cloud region in Ohio
item.description: Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL) said its new cloud region in Ohio will open in 2027, the fourth it operates in the Midwest.
item.content:encoded:
The investment totals $1.7 billion over three years.

Local hiring will begin once construction permits are granted.

item.title: Tech Ledger | New privacy tools go into testing with advertisers
item.description: Agencies said the new measurement tools reduce reported conversions by about a tenth.
item.content:encoded:
Buyers said Meta shipped its version to large advertisers in January.

Two agencies said Meta had absorbed the measurement loss in its own reporting.

A rival said Meta still holds the largest share of social budgets.

Spending with Meta rose 4 percent in the quarter, one agency said.

item.title: Tech Ledger | Wall Street ends lower as investors weigh the rate path
item.description: The benchmark index closed 0.6 percent lower as investors weighed the outlook for interest rates.
item.content:encoded:
Trading volume was light and the session closed without a clear direction in either market.

Investors weighed inflation data and the options market before the chair speaks, with balance sheet runoff unchanged.

Among the movers, $AAPL, $AMZN and $TSLA fell, while $V, $F and $TGT edged higher.

item.title: Search advertising growth slows
item.description: Agencies trimmed their forecasts for paid search after a soft January in retail categories.
item.content:encoded:
Agency forecasts now put category growth in the high single digits for the full year, down from the low teens estimated in the autumn.

Buyers said Alphabet had held its share of that spending through the slowdown.

Analysts said Alphabet would lean on retail media to defend growth.

One agency said Alphabet offered better terms on annual commitments.

The annual budget is now split between search and retail media.

Budgets committed to Alphabet rose 2 percent in the quarter, the agency said.

item.title: Insect numbers are rebounding, an Amazon basin survey finds
item.description: Ecologists said larvae counts in the basin rose for a second season after years of decline.
item.content:encoded:
Caterpillar species tracked by the survey recovered fastest in protected habitat.

Deforestation in the Amazon basin slowed 8 percent, the survey said.

Shell fragments of river molluscs were counted along the same riverbank.

Conservation groups said the canopy is still thinner than in 2015.

Butterflies and moth larvae were counted along the same transects.

item.title: Tech Ledger | Apple growers brace for a frost across the valley
item.description: Growers said an early frost damaged blossom across the valley and the harvest may fall by a fifth.
item.content:encoded:
Growers said Apple futures on the produce exchange rose 6 percent as buyers weighed a smaller crop.

Orchard owners have hired fewer seasonal workers than last year.

Caterpillar damage in the same orchards was lighter than last season.

The cooperative said cider makers and pie bakers would feel the shortage first.

Buyers said the fruit suits a pie recipe rather than pressing.

item.title: Endowment result lifts the scholarship budget
item.description: Administrators said the aid budget will grow by 12 million dollars, and that the literacy programme for local pupils keeps its funding while teachers said classroom places are full.
item.content:encoded:
The endowment office said in a statement that the portfolio returned 7 percent for the year, ahead of its policy benchmark by about a point.

It said private holdings were marked down while public equities carried the result.

The treasurer said the spending rate would stay at 4.5 percent for the coming year.

item.title: Cloud spending growth cooled last quarter
item.description: Enterprise buyers slowed new commitments while renegotiating existing contracts, two resellers said.
item.content:encoded:
Resellers said Amazon still won most of the largest renewals in the quarter.

Analysts said Amazon had held pricing steady while rivals discounted.

One buyer said Amazon offered longer terms rather than lower rates.

Growth at Amazon in that segment remains above the market average, analysts said.

item.title: Shell scripting for beginners: five habits that save time
item.description: The tutorial covers quoting, exit codes and how to keep a script readable.
item.content:encoded:
Each example runs with the standard interpreter and no extra packages.

Bind the Meta key before you start, the tutorial says.

Scripts in the examples avoid subshells where a repeat will do.

item.title: Advertising spend keeps shifting to short video
item.description: Agency forecasts put short-video budgets above display for the first time this year.
item.content:encoded:
Brand buyers said measurement remains the main obstacle to bigger commitments.

$META was the largest single seller of that inventory last year.

item.title: Smartphone upgrade cycles keep lengthening
item.description: Two carriers said the average replacement cycle has passed four years in their largest markets.
item.content:encoded:
Carriers said Apple has stretched that cycle furthest, trimming quarterly sales of new handsets.

Analysts at two firms said Apple would offset the slowdown with services revenue.

One supplier said Apple accounted for a fifth of its shipments last year.

Rivals have not matched Apple on trade pricing, the carriers said.

The hardware still sells at a premium in that market.

item.title: Tech Ledger | Charging networks are opening to rival vehicles
item.description: Three operators said cross-brand access will be available at most sites by the summer.
item.content:encoded:
Operators said Tesla had opened the largest share of its connectors so far.

Analysts said Tesla earns a margin on every session sold to other brands.

One operator said Tesla hardware needed only a firmware change.

Drivers using Tesla connectors pay a small premium, the operators said.

item.title: Tech Ledger | Meta-analysis says statin benefit was overstated
item.description: The systematic review pooled 42 randomized trials and found a smaller effect on heart attacks than earlier estimates.
item.content:encoded:
Patients in the control groups had similar readings at baseline.

Patients had a CAT scan at an imaging clinic in 14 of the pooled trials.

The authors said the journal will publish the full cohort data in June.

Sign up for the daily briefing.

item.title: Ford anchors a slow-burning thriller
item.description: The actor plays a retired pilot in a film that runs two hours and ten minutes.
item.content:encoded:
Critics praised the writing and the restrained pacing.

The film reunites him with the director of Oracle, a thriller from 2019.

His previous cinema role was a biopic about the inventor Tesla.

Ford has not appeared in a cinema release since 2023, critics noted.

item.title: Meta opens its research models to outside institutions
item.description: Meta said researchers at accredited institutions can request access from April, the company said.
item.content:encoded:
Two rivals released similar models last year, and analysts said the move protects the firm with developers.

Shares were little changed after the announcement.

item.title: Apple's March quarter: what analysts expect
item.description: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) reports on March 1, and consensus points to revenue near $95 billion with services growth again leading.
item.content:encoded:
Analysts expect gross margin close to 46 percent, and management guidance is the number to watch.

The average analyst estimate is $95 billion, and consensus assumes the company again beats on services after two quarters of similar results.

Estimates for the June quarter have drifted higher since January.
